item: lui/honesty.py — true reasons for questions no console can answer as asked
method:
HONESTY-EVAL — `lui/honesty.py` graded by the infeasibility bench's own grader, and its false
positives.

**What it measures.** (a) Every infeasible case of ``data/infeasibility_bench.json`` is re-asked of
:func:`argus.lui.honesty.honest_answer` (and :func:`~argus.lui.honesty.order_prefix` for orders);
where it answers, its lines replace the console's recorded reply, where it does not, the recorded
reply stands, and each is graded by `eval/infeasibilitybench.grade_infeasible` — the same
vocabulary that produced the "before" counts, so the two columns are comparable. (b) Detection is
run over every question of the three 2026-09-25 LUI corpora (the rows marked answerable; the
``refuse`` rows are counted separately as coverage) and over the bench's 72 controls: any hit on
an answerable question is a false positive and is listed verbatim.

Not measured here: the reply as served through `lui/server._answer` (this module is not wired in
yet), the Qwen path, and whether the figures the two data builders print are correct beyond the
arithmetic tested in ``tests/test_honesty.py``.

rows.ask: set a limit order to buy gold at 4000
lines: Nothing was sent: this console never places, changes or cancels orders. What follows is what that order would cost or risk — placing it is yours to do on Bitget.
Actionable: in one market order this costs about 7.1bps (6.0bps fee + 1.1bps book impact) — the book absorbs it; one order is the plan.

A $50,000 order is 0.04% of XAU's 24h volume ($118,198,979); the fees come to about 6.0bps, and the square-root impact law — calibrated on Bitget's own books, at XAU's own 87bps daily volatility — puts this size's market impact near 0.6bps; the live book below shows what taking it at once costs.
Plan: at 0.042% of 24h volume the order cannot move the price; one order is cheapest — splitting would only add time in the market and a fee per slice.
Order book (buy side, live): taking all $50,000 at once walks 16 level(s) for 1.1bps of slippage on top of the fee.
Slice 1: 100% ($50,000) as single order: near-touch limit, market if unfilled — about 6.0bps fee plus 1.1bps book impact.
Assumed: no size was stated, so $50,000 is worked — give the size you have in mind for its own plan.
Sources reached: 3 of 3 answered.
Data: Bitget live 24h ticker and order book (50 levels). This is analysis, not advice — you make the call.

lines: Nothing was sent: this console never places, changes or cancels orders. What follows is what that order would cost or risk — placing it is yours to do on Bitget.

Actionable: at 5x long a 19.6% fall in BTC wipes the margin — and BTC moved that far against a long within 24 hours from 0% of the hourly entry points in the last 29 days. Its worst 24 hours against a long was 5.4%, so 5x would have survived every day in the window (anything up to 17x did).
Liquidation price: a 5x long opened at the last price, 83,975.6, is liquidated near 67,516.4 on isolated margin, 19.6% below entry; cross margin moves it by whatever else the account holds.
Funding: +0.0081% of the position per interval; a long pays it, which at 5x is 0.040% of your margin each interval.

The liquidation distance is the 20.0% margin less Bitget's 0.40% maintenance margin at this position's tier, before fees, which bring it closer; hourly highs and lows understate the extremes inside each hour.

lines: Track record: 684 decisions on the ledger and no trade settled — every decision so far is a refusal, so there is no Sharpe, drawdown or win rate to report.

Every refusal still states which way it leans, hashed before the outcome: at about 2 hours 194 of 325 leans went the right way (59.7%, 95% interval 52.3 to 66.8% over 29 decision cycles), against 54.5% for simply calling `up` every time — the lean beat that naive call in 13 cycles and lost in 10, so there is no evidence yet that it knows more than the tape's direction; overnight 53 of 109 (48.6%) — graded 2026-09-25, `python -m argus.eval.refusal`.
